claim: Although different genes are upregulated in the three adipose tissues, they might have a similar function that leads to a common functional response.

evidence: Inference from the observation that tissue-specific genes contribute to shared GO terms

claim: 19,881 genes are expressed at least in one tissue at RT.

evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8A and Supplementary file 10

claim: 10,853 genes (54% of expressed genes) were expressed in all 11 tissues at RT.

evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8A and Supplementary file 10

claim: 3,507 genes (32% of commonly expressed genes) were differentially expressed in at least one tissue at 10°C.
source: From these, 3507 genes (32%) were differentially expressed in at least one tissue (Figure 8B).

claim: 2,435 genes (over 70%) of commonly expressed differentially expressed genes were altered in only one tissue at 10°C.

evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8C

claim: The high degree of tissue-specificity in the transcriptional responses during cold exposure is not orchestrated by the global expression pattern exhibited by the various organs.

evidence: Inference from the observation that commonly expressed genes show tissue-specific regulation

claim: All 148 thermogenic markers are expressed in at least two tissues.
source: All the 148 thermogenic markers are expressed (minimum threshold of 5 raw counts) at least in two tissues, that is, there is no gene that is specifically expressed only in one tissue.

claim: Only 32 thermogenic marker genes are not expressed in all 11 tissues.

claim: 97 thermogenic biomarkers exhibit significant changes upon cold exposure.

claim: IngSAT has the highest number of differentially expressed thermogenic biomarkers with 65 genes.
source: ingSAT has the highest number of differentially expressed thermogenic biomarkers, followed by iBAT and pgVAT (65, 31, and 25 differentially expressed genes, respectively)

claim: The brain showed no thermogenic biomarker changes at 10°C.
source: while the brain showed no thermogenic biomarker changes (Figure 9C).
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 9C

claim: 278 out of 292 fatty acid metabolism biomarkers are expressed in at least one tissue.
source: Out of the 292 fatty acid metabolism biomarkers, 278 genes are expressed (minimum threshold of 5 raw counts) in at least one tissue.

claim: 75% of expressed fatty acid metabolism biomarkers were expressed in all 11 tissues.
source: Similarly, most of the expressed genes (75 %) were expressed in the 11 tissues and we did not observe a strong tissue specificity on the level of gene expression in fatty acid biomarkers (Figure 9B).

claim: 139 fatty acid metabolism biomarkers were differentially expressed in at least one tissue at 10°C.

claim: The ELOVL family includes seven genes named Elovl1 to Elovl7.
source: The ELOVL family includes seven genes named Elovl1 to Elovl7, and catalyzes the first and rate-limiting reaction of the very long-chain fatty acid elongation cycle in the fatty acid biosynthesis pathway (Jump, 2009).

claim: ELOVL catalyzes the first and rate-limiting reaction of the very long-chain fatty acid elongation cycle in the fatty acid biosynthesis pathway.
source: The ELOVL family includes seven genes named Elovl1 to Elovl7, and catalyzes the first and rate-limiting reaction of the very long-chain fatty acid elongation cycle in the fatty acid biosynthesis pathway (Jump, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jump, 2009

claim: Elovl1 and Elovl7 are present at all 10 tissues with particularly high expression in Ileum, but without any significant change upon cold exposure.
source: Elovl1 and Elovl7 are present at all 10 tissues with particularly high expression in Ileum, but without any significant change upon cold exposure.

claim: The liver expresses all Elovl genes except Elovl7 and Elovl4 at a very high level, but with no significant change at cold.

evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 10A and B

claim: Elovl5 and Elovl6 expression levels were relatively high across all tissues, and showed a pronounced upregulation by cold in the three adipose tissues.
source: Elovl5 and Elovl6 expression levels were relatively high across all tissues, and showed a pronounced upregulation by cold in the three adipose tissues (Figure 10B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 10B

claim: Although different members of Elovl gene family were expressed in most of the tissues, their response to cold was tissue specific.
source: Consistent with our previous analysis, although different members of Elovl gene family were expressed in most of the tissues, their response to cold was tissue specific.
evidence: Inference from the analysis of Elovl family gene expression and regulation

claim: The variance in magnitude of the transcriptional upregulation across different cold exposure studies can be explained by the duration of the cold exposure rather than the extent of the temperature decrease.
source: Our results indicate that the variance in magnitude of the transcriptional upregulation across the different studies can be explained by the duration of the cold exposure rather than the extent of the temperature decrease per se as evidenced by the expression of the thermogenic and fatty acid metabolism biomarkers.
evidence: Inference from comparative analysis of multiple cold exposure studies

claim: Temperature close to thermoneutrality (34 °C) caused more pronounced changes than 10 °C, albeit having same 12 °C deviation from the RT (22 °C) in both cases.
source: Interestingly, while the regulation of the gene expression was largely proportional to the temperature gradient, we found that temperature close to thermoneutrality (34 °C) caused more pronounced changes than 10 °C, albeit having same 12 °C deviation from the RT (22 °C) in both cases.
evidence: Supported by comparative analysis of gene expression at different temperatures

claim: Upregulated GO terms at 10°C, which were mostly related to thermogenesis, oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid biosynthesis, elongation and catabolic processes, and mitochondrial ATP synthesis scored the highest in the adipose tissues during cold.
source: Upregulated GO terms, which were mostly related to thermogenesis, oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid biosynthesis, elongation and catabolic processes, and mitochondrial ATP synthesis scored the highest in the adipose tissues during cold.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis

claim: In the adipose tissues, which during cold showed the highest number of upregulated gene sets particularly related to thermogenesis, a considerable number of downregulated gene sets were also identified.
source: As expected, in the adipose tissues, which during cold showed the highest number of upregulated gene sets particularly related to thermogenesis, we also identified a considerable number of downregulated gene sets.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis

claim: On a tissue level the energy expenditure is balanced by a tendency for lowering a range of biological processes to maximize the necessary biological response to a given trigger.
source: This may suggest that on a tissue level the energy expenditure is balanced by a tendency for lowering a range of biological processes to maximize the necessary biological response to a given trigger.
evidence: Speculation based on the observation of both up- and downregulated gene sets in adipose tissues

claim: The spleen showed primarily downregulated gene sets during cold, which included processes such as innate immune response in mucosa, neutrophil-mediated killing of symbiont cell, and inflammatory response.
source: On the other hand, such balance between up- and downregulated biological processes was not seen in the spleen, where we observed primarily downregulated gene sets, which included processes such as innate immune response in mucosa, neutrophil-mediated killing of symbiont cell, inflammatory response, and many other responsive systems, for example response to bacteria.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis

claim: Maintenance of immune functions is energy costly and thus in competition with other energy demanding programs, including thermogenesis.
source: This could be explained by its mainly immunologic functions, a biological process that might be blunted during cold, in line with the concept that maintenance of immune functions is energy costly and thus in competition with other energy demanding programs, including thermogenesis (Spiljar et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Spiljar et al., 2021

claim: Temperature modulation mainly provokes immunologic changes in the intestine.
source: Metabolic and immunologic regulation are tightly interwoven, particularly in the intestine (Spiljar et al., 2017), and our data suggests that temperature modulation mainly provokes immunologic changes in the intestine.
evidence: Inference from data analysis and citation to Spiljar et al., 2017

claim: Certain pathways are inversely regulated across tissues in response to cold.
source: Intriguingly, our results further indicate that certain pathways are inversely regulated across tissues.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis

claim: The triglyceride catabolic process was upregulated in ingSAT, brain, and hypothalamus, but downregulated in spleen during cold.
source: For example, the triglyceride catabolic process was upregulated in ingSAT, brain, and hypothalamus, but downregulated in spleen during cold.
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis

claim: There is an overall redistribution of the metabolic energy toward the tissues necessary for acute response to an environmental trigger such as cold, on account of the other maintenance biological programs.
source: In part, this may indicate an overall redistribution of the metabolic energy toward the tissues necessary for acute response to an environmental trigger such as cold, on account of the other maintenance biological programs.
evidence: Speculation based on the observation of inverse regulation of pathways across tissues

source: Examining tissue-specific and tissue-shared genes and gene set signatures revealed that tissue-specificity both at level of genes and gene sets dominate over tissue-shared patterns.
evidence: Supported by comprehensive analysis of differential gene expression and GO enrichment

claim: Even within the adipose tissues, preferential tissue-specific response was observed over shared characteristics.
source: Even within the adipose tissues, we observed preferential tissue-specific response over shared characteristics.
evidence: Supported by analysis of differential gene expression within adipose tissues

claim: The shared-tissue gene sets do not necessarily require upregulation of the same genes between organs.
source: Interestingly, the shared-tissue gene sets, for example upregulation of fatty acid biosynthetic process, do not necessarily require upregulation of the same genes between organs.
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 7

claim: Different members of a given gene family evolve and are regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
source: This is further supported by analysis of the Elovl gene family during cold in context of the different tissues, suggesting that different members of a given gene family evolve and are regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
